podcast.body: A single from the 1981 album "Wild-Eyed Southern Boys," this song was a major hit for the band, reaching number three on the charts. Its success was attributed to a shift in their sound, designed to appeal to radio, and the emergence of MTV. The song has a noticeable stylistic similarity to The Cars' "Just What I Needed." "the single Hold on loosely made it to number three."

podcast.body: This song was released in 1981 on the album "Wild-Eyed Southern Boys" and became a major hit, reaching number three on the charts. Its success was bolstered by its radio omnipresence and regular video rotation on MTV, which debuted in the same year. The song's opening riff notably "borrow[ed] a little something from the cars," specifically resembling "Just What I Needed." The sound of the song marked a shift towards "arena rock" rather than traditional Southern rock. "Just hold on, loose, baby. Don't let go. If you quit, do something. You're going to lose control."
